truths.truth: Every test contract reads a frame's or a slice's end through the time base and judges times exactly, with no tolerance
truths.evidence: tests/js/contracts/picture.js:184, :188 and :189 compute a slice's end as `slices[j].at + slices[j].ms` and keep `const EPS = 1e-9` (:38), applied to ms overlaps at :192 and :194. Production slices carry `end`, with `ms = p.end - p.at` (store/meter/spectrogram.js:98-106), and slicerange.js:39 reads `endOf(s)`. So the test oracle (columnSlices, used by picture-probes.js:165) derives the same instant differently from the code under test and needs a tolerance to agree with it. tests/js/store/meter/loop.test.js:101-102 also derives slice ends and joins as `at + ms` instead of endOf.
